mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, eroding corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over the same month indicates a housing demand shock with weak overall demand, which depresses consumer confidence and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS and a decrease in UNRATE over two months signals a situation of rising employment but stagnant wage growth, which constrains consumer spending and corporate pricing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly CPIAUCSL above 2.5% for four consecutive months signals persistent inflation, prompting expectations of future rate hikes and higher discount rates, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 and RSAFS over two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand and savings, which reduces corporate revenue and cash flow, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous month AND RSAFS < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
